title: The Hollow of Caerlum
premise: Emrys Marchetti, an exiled storm-caller, has spent a lifetime hiding in the valley of Caerlum, where magic cannot follow and the old gods have long been silent. When prayers begin to be answered again, Emrys learns the valley's silence was a covenant they unknowingly inherited from their grandmother, one that sealed the realms apart at the cost of the last dragon-fire. With a runaway shrine-keeper named Wren and the ghost-memory of the dragon Vaelith, Emrys must journey beyond the valley to reforge the broken covenant before the fire gutters out and both realms go dark. In the end, Emrys chooses not to restore the old order but to write a new covenant with found family as its witnesses, trading their exile for a home that holds them by choice.
about_author: Rosalind Sterling is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk songs about vanished gods before turning to fiction. They write from a drafty cottage in the hills, accompanied by an opinionated cat and an ever-growing collection of mismatched teacups.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: introduces Caerlum, where magic cannot follow and Emrys's storm-calling lies dormant. A prayer whispered at a dead shrine is answered for the first time in decades. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine, the first crack in a carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Wren, POV: a runaway shrine-keeper arrives in Caerlum carrying a censer of dragon-fire ash that still glows. She recognizes Emrys's bloodline mark from temple records. Emotional beat: wary curiosity between two people who both fled something.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Buried
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: searching their grandmother's house, Emrys finds a covenant-stone hidden under the hearth, inscribed with the Marchetti name as guarantor of the valley's silence. Emotional beat: grief curdling into betrayal; inheritance revealed as a burden.

chapters.title: The God Who Answers
chapters.summary: Dual POV: a minor god manifests in Wren's dreams, begging them to carry word to the dying dragon Vaelith. The god warns the covenant is failing. Emotional beat: awe and terror; the sacred intruding on the mundane.

chapters.title: Leaving Caerlum
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: crossing the valley boundary, magic floods back into Emrys painfully after decades of dormancy. Their first uncontrolled storm nearly kills them both. Emotional beat: exhilaration laced with fear; power returning like feeling to a numb limb.

chapters.title: Road of Small Prayers
chapters.summary: Wren, POV: traveling through villages where answered prayers have bred desperation and cults. Wren's shrine-keeping skills save them from a mob. Emotional beat: disillusionment with faith, tempered by small kindnesses.

chapters.title: The Hollow Choir
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: the pair shelters with a commune of exiled mages who worship the silence itself and want the covenant kept broken. Their leader offers Emrys belonging—at the price of abandoning Wren. Emotional beat: temptation of easy family versus hard truth.

chapters.title: Vaelith's First Memory
chapters.summary: Vaelith (ghost-memory), POV: flashback chapter revealing the original covenant—forged when gods and mortals warred, sealed by a dragon's sacrifice of her own fire. Emotional beat: ancient sorrow; love weaponized into law.

chapters.title: Smoke Without Fire
chapters.summary: Wren, POV: they reach the dragon-hollow and find Vaelith's flame guttering, her body half-dissolved into memory. She can only speak through borrowed recollections. Emotional beat: tenderness toward something vast and dying.

chapters.title: The Price of Reforging
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: Vaelith explains the covenant can only be remade by a blood-guarantor willing to anchor it with their own memory—the price Emrys's grandmother refused to pay alone. Emotional beat: horror at the cost; resolve forming anyway.

chapters.title: Hollow Men Marching
chapters.summary: Dual POV: the Hollow Choir, learning of the quest, marches to destroy Vaelith and preserve the silence. Villages along the route turn hostile as gods grow louder and stranger. Emotional beat: rising dread; the world choosing sides.

chapters.title: Storm Over Saltmarsh
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: ambushed at a river crossing, Emrys fully awakens their storm-calling to save Wren, leveling the marsh. They are horrified by their own strength. Emotional beat: power as identity crisis; Wren's loyalty steadying them.

chapters.title: The Shrine Beneath the Lake
chapters.summary: Wren, POV: seeking a relic needed for the rite, Wren confronts the temple she fled and the mentor who betrayed her. She takes the relic and forgives neither of them. Emotional beat: reclaiming agency without cheap absolution.

chapters.title: Gods in the Grain
chapters.summary: Vaelith, POV: the old gods stir restlessly as the covenant weakens, some wanting freedom, some wanting dominion. Vaelith bargains with three of them for time. Emotional beat: political tension among immortals; hope bought on credit.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: campfire interlude. Emrys and Wren trade the memories each would hate to lose, realizing how much of themselves they've already sacrificed. Emotional beat: intimacy deepening into chosen family; quiet before catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Choir Arrives
chapters.summary: Dual POV: the Hollow Choir reaches the hollow, led by its charismatic leader wielding stolen silence-magic. Vaelith's last defenders fall. Emotional beat: siege terror; allies becoming strangers.

chapters.title: Guttering
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: Vaelith's flame nearly dies mid-battle; the leader shatters the old covenant-stone, unleashing raw divine chaos across the land. Emotional beat: despair at rock bottom; everything Emrys inherited now rubble.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: Climax, Emrys POV: Emrys offers their memories as the new anchor while Wren channels the final flame through the relic. Together they kindle a new covenant—not silence, but witness—binding realms in mutual recognition. Emotional beat: self-sacrifice transfigured into authorship.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Wren, POV: the battle ends; the Choir leader, shown the new covenant's mercy, breaks rather than burns. Gods withdraw to honored distance instead of exile. Emotional beat: exhausted relief; mercy as victory.

chapters.title: The Memory I Chose to Lose
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: Emrys wakes missing pieces—a childhood face, a bitter year—but keeps what matters most. Vaelith, reborn small as an ember-wyrm, curls in their pocket. Emotional beat: bittersweet wholeness; loss accepted as the shape of choice.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Unhidden
chapters.summary: Dual POV: they return to Caerlum, which remembers them now, and find villagers waiting—not with torches but with questions and open doors. Emrys calls a gentle rain just to feel it. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not inherited.

chapters.title: A New Covenant Written
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating voices: months later, Emrys, Wren, and the ember-wyrm establish a school at the old shrine where magic and memory are taught openly. The final lines echo the book's first prayer—this time answered by human hands. Emotional beat: hopeful closure; legacy rewritten as gift.
